title: Encoder unwrapping can alias on fast motion
evidence: "unwrapping assumes less than half a counter revolution between samples, nothing checks it" (crates/device/src/lib.rs:196-197); the servo loop also "never catches up after an overrun" (apps/calibration/src/worker.rs:1318-1320), so sampling gaps are possible.
failure: a fast hand motion or a scheduling stall exceeds half a revolution; the delta wraps the wrong way; position jumps by a full revolution's worth — in a future bridge this becomes a wild node drag (graph data corruption), in calibration a phantom excursion.

title: No hardware watchdog: a frozen host leaves the last force latched
evidence: "expiry is only evaluated when the worker runs, there is no hardware watchdog" (crates/device/src/lib.rs:59-60, docs/spec/12-force-feedback.md:91-92); "It cannot protect against the computer itself freezing or the process being killed, because no timer lives in the hardware" (VT-02, For the business).
failure: a host scheduler stall or process kill leaves the last motor packet applied indefinitely; the arm holds force with no software running to remove it — the exact failure the envelope exists to prevent.

title: A failed shutdown cannot be retried by Drop
evidence: "end_force_session clears the pending sequence even when shutdown failed, so Drop cannot resend neutral packets, it only retries the port release" (crates/hal/src/device.rs:345, :326-328).
failure: the two neutral `0xc5` packets are lost mid-shutdown; Drop cannot retry them; the device is left with the last written offsets and an unhealthy connection needing a full reconnect; if the operator-side recovery is missed, nonzero offsets persist.

title: On Wayland the hold interlock can read held forever
evidence: "on Wayland a held Space can stay latched after focus loss because no key-up or focus event arrives, only the 250 ms heartbeat and Stop remain" (apps/calibration/src/main.rs:295-302).
failure: during the owner session the window loses focus while held; the hold interlock — a primary operator stop — is effectively absent for the remainder of the attempt, leaving heartbeat and Stop as the only defences.

failure: a refactor breaks the hold-release or stale-heartbeat wiring outside the controller unit; `cargo test` and the smoke run stay green; the fault is first seen at the arm.
